title: CLARITY Act Back on Track
author: Sigma Capital
metaDescription: The CLARITY Act is back on track in the Senate, but no markup date has been set. Major U.S. banks oppose the new proposal. The bill's future remains uncertain.

body: # CLARITY Act: The Senate Is Back. Tim Scott has not set a markup date. Here is where the CLARITY Act stands. **Join the FinTech Weekly Clarity Circle →**. Senator Lummis posted three words on X this afternoon, the day the Senate returned from Easter recess. The Banking Committee's markup window is now open. Whether Chairman Tim Scott puts a date on it is the only question that matters this week. It is also, **as FinTech Weekly reported before the recess**, the version Coinbase told Senate staff it could not support after reviewing the March 23 draft. As FinTech Weekly mapped, the composition of the President's Council of Advisors on Science and Technology (**PCAST**) reflects where the White House sits on the remaining substantive questions. CLARITY Act: Garlinghouse Said April, Then May. The Bill Still Has No Markup Date. The Senate Banking Committee still has not set a date. The Markup Date Has Not. CLARITY Act: The Obstacle Changed This Week.
Major U.S. banking groups are pushing back against new stablecoin rules in the CLARITY Act, warning that the latest proposal does not go far
